key_insight: Grain-boundary segregation in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni delays the onset of plastic flow, mainly by slowing early deformation rather than changing dislocation content.
engineering_relevance: Tuning grain-boundary chemistry in nanocrystalline stainless alloys could improve early-stage strength and delay yielding under high stress.
method: Hybrid molecular dynamics/Monte Carlo simulations on three nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni polycrystals
Compared segregated structures against annealed and random controls using the same microstructures
Evaluated response under constant uniaxial stress and fixed strain-rate loading across 300–950 K
evidence_signal: Under 4.6 GPa at 300 K, segregated polycrystals reached 50% strain about 16% later than random ones, and at fixed strain rate they showed a 6–7% higher peak stress than annealed controls across 300, 750, and 950 K.
watch_item: The reported Cr enrichment depends strongly on the chosen reference region, so interpretation of segregation metrics must be consistent.
paper_title: Grain-boundary segregation delays the onset of plastic flow in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni
